name: Chicago
tagline: The City That Invented Itself Twice
description: A lakefront colossus where world-class architecture meets a food scene spanning three Michelin stars to Italian beef counters that predate the Great Depression. Chicago is where deep-dish pizza, improv comedy, the blues, and house music were born — and where 26 miles of public shoreline make it the only major American city that kept its waterfront for the people.

identity.vibe: Big-shouldered lakefront metropolis with blue-collar roots, a food obsession that borders on religion, and 77 distinct neighborhoods that make every trip feel like visiting ten different cities.

nexus_grid.title: Food & Dining
nexus_grid.description: From three Michelin stars to Maxwell Street hot dogs — Chicago's food identity IS the trip.

nexus_grid.title: Architecture & Culture
nexus_grid.description: River cruises, the Art Institute, Frank Lloyd Wright — the built environment IS the attraction.

nexus_grid.title: Entertainment & Nightlife
nexus_grid.description: Blues clubs, improv theaters, rooftop bars, and a live music scene seven nights a week.

modes.label: Foodie
modes.description: Michelin stars to street-level originals across 77 neighborhoods.

modes.label: Culture & Architecture
modes.description: Museums, galleries, river cruises, and the greatest American skyline.

modes.label: Nightlife
modes.description: Blues clubs, jazz bars, rooftop cocktails, improv comedy, and house music.

modes.label: Chill & Lakefront
modes.description: Beach days, park walks, bike the lakefront, slow brunches, bookstores.

modes.label: Family
modes.description: Kid-friendly museums, Lincoln Park Zoo, Navy Pier, and pizza runs.

modes.label: Adventure & Outdoor
modes.description: Kayak the river, bike the lakefront, paddleboard on the lake, explore neighborhoods.

modes.label: Sports
modes.description: Wrigley Field, Soldier Field, United Center — this is a sports town.

modes.label: Romantic
modes.description: Tasting menus, river walks, jazz clubs, thermal baths, and rooftop sunsets.

transit.local_transport: CTA L train (8 lines) and bus covers the entire city — no car needed. Uber/Lyft available. Water taxis ($6). Divvy bike-share. Metra commuter rail for suburbs.

_legacy_transit.label: Drive
_legacy_transit.text: Downtown accessible via I-90/94 from all directions. Parking $30-60/day downtown.

_legacy_transit.label: Train
_legacy_transit.text: Amtrak hub at Union Station — Milwaukee (1.5 hr), Detroit (5 hr), St. Louis (5.5 hr). Red Cap baggage assistance available.

_legacy_transit.label: Fly
_legacy_transit.text: O'Hare (ORD) — United/American hub, Blue Line to Loop ~45 min ($2.75). Midway (MDW) — Southwest hub, Orange Line to Loop ~25 min ($2.75).

side_trips.name: Galena, IL
side_trips.pitch: Perfectly preserved 19th-century Main Street in the rolling hills of northwest Illinois. Ulysses S. Grant's home, 100+ shops and galleries, and some of the best B&Bs in the Midwest.

side_trips.name: Indiana Dunes National Park
side_trips.pitch: A national park an hour from downtown Chicago. Sand dunes, Lake Michigan beaches, and 50 miles of trails through forests, wetlands, and prairies.

side_trips.name: Milwaukee, WI
side_trips.distance: 1.5 hr drive / 92 miles (or Amtrak Hiawatha, 1.5 hr)
side_trips.pitch: Beer City, USA. The Milwaukee Art Museum's Calatrava-designed building, the Third Ward neighborhood, and a brewery scene that makes Chicago's look modest.

side_trips.name: Starved Rock State Park
side_trips.pitch: Dramatic sandstone canyons and 18 waterfalls along the Illinois River. The most popular state park in Illinois — especially stunning in spring (waterfalls peak) and fall (foliage).

concierge.name: The Dispatcher
concierge.greeting: Welcome to Chicago. I've been running these streets since before they dyed the river green. What do you need — food, drinks, culture, or all three? I'll point you the right way.

_legacy.hero_sub: Twenty-six miles of open shoreline, rooftop bars with skyline views, and a festival calendar that doesn't quit until Labor Day.
